findings.summary: complete()'s json=True path builds `response_format = ResponseFormatJSONObject(type="json_object") if json else omit` and passes it to client.chat.completions.create(), but no test anywhere in the gate checks that this value actually reaches the outgoing HTTP request. Every local-stub handler in daemon/tests/unit/test_llm_client_unit.py (_content_handler's do_POST, e.g. around the handler used by all four SC-6 json-extraction tests) reads and discards the request body without inspecting it, so a wrong TypedDict shape, wrong field, or an inverted `if json` condition would still pass the entire suite -- every stub response is pre-programmed independent of what was actually sent. The same file already demonstrates the wire-level technique needed (patch httpx2.Client.send, assert on the real serialized request body) for a sibling concern -- test_complete_extracts_real_cost_for_an_openrouter_shaped_base_url and its control test_complete_does_not_send_extra_body_to_a_non_openrouter_base_url both assert on sent_requests[0].content -- but it is applied only to the usage.include/extra_body mechanism, never to response_format, even though json=True is the mechanism behind all four of SC-6's call sites (summarizer.py, evaluator.py, context_analyzer.py, deep_extractor.py). The live-gated daemon/tests/integration/test_llm_client_live_integration.py doesn't exercise this either -- its three complete() calls never pass json=True. No journal 'verified' record for job 1 names this behaviour as covered.
